plan.notes: Sources: (1) TCNJ 2026-2027 Undergraduate Bulletin, Computer Science section, 'SUGGESTED COURSE SEQUENCE FOR BS IN COMPUTER SCIENCE (30 units)' (bulletin PDF pages CS-13/CS-14; https://bulletin.tcnj.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/80/2026/06/Computer-Science-2026.pdf); (2) Dept. of Computer Science 'Suggested Sequence for Computer Science Majors' PDF, updated 2026 (https://computerscience.tcnj.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/205/2026/07/Computer-Science-Suggested-Sequence-2026-final.pdf), which provides the official Fall/Spring split for Years 2-4. Degree verified: the TRUE degree is the B.S. in Computer Science (bulletin: 'The Department of Computer Science offers the B.S. degree in Computer Science'; program accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET). No silent substitution. Transcription method: downloaded both PDFs via curl on 2026-09-30 and manually transcribed every sequence cell (course code, title, units) into this file; Fall/Spring splits taken verbatim from the dept PDF's two-column layout; per-term and total units re-verified against the bulletin's printed year totals. TCNJ uses course units: 1 unit = 4 credit hours (per dept sequence note); 0.25-unit seminars = 1 credit; CSC 099 (0 units) is a required 0-credit course flagged required_zero. CREDIT-TOTAL DISCREPANCY (documented honestly): the catalog degree minimum is 30 units (120 credits), but the official suggested sequence's own printed year totals are 8 + 8.25 + 8.25 + 6 = 30.5 units = 122 credits. Per pipeline rule, total_credits is set to the sequence's OWN published total (122). The extra 0.5 unit comes from the three required seminar courses (CSC 099 at 0 units, CSC 199 and CSC 299 at 0.25 units each). Caveats: (a) The published sequence does not list per-course prerequisites, so all prereq arrays are intentionally empty -- no prerequisites invented; the published term ordering preserves the prerequisite chain. (b) Choice-slot titles/codes are the sequence's own either/or wording; placeholder codes (e.g. WLANG-1, CORE-1, SCI-1, ELECT-FREE-1, CSC OPT-1) are distinct per slot and never reused. (c) CSC 220 is CS I (per bulletin requirements section and dept PDF; the bulletin sequence page labels it 'CS II', which appears to be a catalog typo -- CSC 230 is CS II: Data Structures). (d) World-language placement: students continuing a second language must take a placement test; two courses or up to level 103, whichever comes first. (e) This plan is the plain B.S. in Computer Science track only; the bulletin also publishes separate sequences for the Data Science and Cybersecurity specializations and the Seven-Year B.S./M.D. program -- not transcribed here. (f) Grade rule per bulletin: C or higher required in CSC 220, CSC 230, CSC 270, CSC 335, and MAT 127.
